feedback: Reject: the RM does not encode the task's core requirement. 'Be holding the key on at least two different moves' means two separate holding episodes - acquire the key, lose it, acquire it again - which is exactly what the `key_lost` event exists to mark (it fires on the one drop step while the door is still closed). The candidate never uses `key_lost`. Because `has_door_key` is a persistent condition (true on every step the key is carried), the transition (u2, has_door_key) -> u3 fires on the very next step after (u1, has_door_key) -> u2 whenever the agent simply keeps carrying, so the 0.2 is collected with no loss and no re-acquisition. Counterexample: the environment's own example trace (key picked up at step 12, carried through the toggle at step 17, dropped at step 19) is a single continuous holding, yet it walks u0->u1->u2->u3->u4->u5 and collects the full 1.7 - under the intended reading it violates the task (the only loss happens while the door is open, so key_lost never fires). The lenient reading ('held on >=2 distinct steps') cannot be intended: every box-pickup trace necessarily holds the key from pickup through the toggle (pickup step and toggle step are distinct), so that reading would make the first clause redundant and the task collapse to the base 'pick up the box' task. Fix direction: make the has_door_key regression explicit by replacing the blocker_moved/second-has_door_key pair with an event transition between the two holdings, i.e. a chain of the form has_door_key -> key_lost -> has_door_key -> door_open -> target_picked_up (6 states with per-state else self-loops); since key_lost's definition requires the door closed, the loss must occur before opening, which both the key-first and ball-first orders can satisfy, so reachability is preserved and 'at least two' is honored via else self-loops on further loss/re-hold cycles. Secondary issue: (u0, blocker_moved) -> u1 imposes a blocker-before-key ordering the task never states and leaves the first holding of the natural key-first strategy uncounted; the holdings themselves should drive the chain. Otherwise the artifact is sound: exact header format, FINAL_STATES present with declared accepting u5, else self-loops in every state covering irrelevant events, predicate-only labels, non-negative bounded dense rewards, and the machine is completable.

feedback: Reject: the automaton over-constrains the task and yields no terminal reward on canonical solutions. The task requires has_door_key to hold at two distinct moves plus the box pickup; it never requires the key to be lost, let alone lost while the door is still closed. Yet u1 is exitable only via key_lost, which by definition fires only on the single step where the key is dropped with door_open false. Any solution that unlocks the door while carrying the key and then drops it (key_lost stays false because the door is open) is trapped in u1 forever: the subsequent door_open and target_picked_up steps are swallowed by (u1, else). The seed-0 example trace is exactly this case — key held from step 12 through 18 (seven different moves), door toggled at 17 while carrying, key dropped at 19 with the door open, box picked up at 28 — and under this RM it earns at most 0.15 and never reaches u5. The minimal solution (move the ball aside, pick up the key, toggle while holding it, drop the key, grab the box) fails identically. Even under a charitable 'two separate holds' reading the RM is wrong: a second hold after a door-open drop satisfies the task but is unreachable here, because key_lost can never fire once the door has been open. The two holding moves must be counted by chaining has_door_key twice — (u0, has_door_key)->u1 then (u1, has_door_key)->u2 — which fires on the second step at which the key is held, whether that hold is continuous or interrupted by a drop with the door open or closed; key_lost must not gate the path. Otherwise the artifact is largely sound: per-state else self-loops cover irrelevant events, key_lost is correctly handled as a one-step event rather than a latch, progress rewards are dense, bounded, and terminal-dominant (0.6 total before the 1.0), FINAL_STATES is present with u5 declared and accepting, all states are reachable, and omitting blocker_moved is safe since door_open implies it by environment dynamics.

Semantic fidelity: the chain (u0,has_door_key)->u1 and (u1,has_door_key)->u2 counts has_door_key true on two distinct moves; consecutive holding steps legitimately count as two different moves, and the task does not require losing the key in between, so else self-loops (no regression on key drop) are the correct treatment rather than a missing explicit regression. door_open as an intermediate is safe: target_picked_up can never precede door_open (the box room has no other entrance), so inserting it preserves the accepted language exactly while giving a denser shaping ladder; blocker_moved is rightly not rewarded since it is not part of the task. Reachability: the key is obtainable without moving the ball (u0->u1); one further holding step reaches u2; from u2 the agent can drop the key, move the ball, re-pick the key, and toggle (u3); from u3 drop the key and pick up the box (u4) — all well within the 576-step limit, and the seed-0 trace (steps 12, 13, 17, 28) exercises every transition. Ordered coverage is consistent with the environment's hard constraints: the toggle step itself carries has_door_key, so the u1->u2 transition fires there if needed and persistent door_open triggers u2->u3 the next step (door_open cannot be re-shut), so no successful episode can dead-end in u1; target_picked_up is last-step-only and correctly gates the final transition, with the key necessarily dropped first (has_door_key and target_picked_up never co-occur). Predicate-only labels throughout; the event key_lost and the unused blocker_moved are relegated to per-state else self-loops, which cover all irrelevant propositions in every state; persistent/event semantics are respected. Format is exact: STATES, INITIAL_STATE, a nonempty FINAL_STATES header (u4, declared and accepting), TRANSITION_FUNCTION with per-state else self-loops, and REWARD_FUNCTION covering all progress transitions.

feedback: All five environment-declared propositions are implemented and the function set is exactly the declared set (blocker_moved, has_door_key, door_open, target_picked_up, key_lost); no undeclared extras, no missing predicates, no imports, no mutations or side effects, and the code is syntactically valid. blocker_moved: instead of locating the single door and testing its front cell, the predicate scans all cells and, for any cell holding a door with x>0, checks the cell at (x-1, y) for a ball. Since the environment has exactly one door at (dx, dy) with dx >= 2 and the front/start-side cell is (dx-1, dy), this is semantically equivalent to the reference expression: true iff no ball sits at (dx-1, dy). A ball in hand is off-grid and counts as moved; dropping the ball back on that cell makes it false again, matching the non-latch condition reading. Guards (x > 0, cell is not None, neighbor is not None) prevent any None dereference and out-of-range access, and grid reads are side-effect free. has_door_key, door_open, and target_picked_up are verbatim matches to the documented expressions (carrying key with color matching the door found by type scan; any door with is_open; carrying box with mission string 'pick up the {color} box', so the mission's designated box is matched rather than a fixed color). key_lost implements the event correctly: previous valuation read-only access to env.episode_memory['previous_valuation'], requires prev['has_door_key'] true, re-evaluates the current has_door_key expression (K) and door_open expression (D) and requires both false. The leading truthiness guard on the previous valuation is harmless because the valuation is a complete, non-empty dict, and it short-circuits safely if absent; the event is true for exactly the one step after the key is dropped with the door closed and false otherwise, so it never co-occurs with has_door_key, door_open, or target_picked_up. Persistent predicates read only current state; the event only reads the prior snapshot; nothing writes to the environment or episode memory.
